lastCommit.message:
[ota-hal] OTA-1657: the healing pouch, and three racks that fold

Owner: "battle gets slowed down when you have to heal. let's make it available
from the exploration screen. let's make another bandolier and call it the healing
pouch or something. and we can load it with any three healing items they want so
in an out 5 trauma kits, say 3 trail rations and maybe 10 blueberries in it. and
we open it like a bandolier during combat and can use the preloaded heals from
there. and when you use it, it acts like they do when being used from inventory."

And, a moment later: "when you are in inventory let's make the bandolier, tool
pouch and healing pouch collapsable like inventory categories to save space."

⚠ THREE POCKETS, AND A POCKET IS A STACK. That distinction is the whole feature
and it is why his exact load-out fits in three: a racked id points at an
inventory STACK, so "Blueberries ×10" is ONE pocket you can tap ten times, not
ten pockets. It is the same storage contract the bandolier has had since arb110 —
the items never leave `player.inventory`, the rack only records WHICH STACKS are
within reach — so nothing is duplicated, nothing can be lost by racking, and a
stack spent by any other path simply stops resolving instead of holding a pocket
hostage as a ghost (OTA-1005's lesson from the tool pouch, applied up front).

⚠⚠ THE TAP CALLS `useInventoryItem`, AND THAT IS THE POINT. He said it should act
"like they do when being used from inventory" — so it is not "like", it is the
SAME action the pack's USE button fires. The heal, the stamina, the cure, the
stack decrement, the Arbiter's line and every downstream hook stay one
implementation. A second copy of "what eating a Trauma Kit does" is precisely the
class of drift the last three OTAs have been spent removing.

⚠ AND ELIGIBILITY DELEGATES RATHER THAN DECIDING. `consumableDoesSomething`
already answers "does this mend, restore, cleanse or cure?", and it exists
because a pure antivenom (healHP 0, cure yes) was once accepted by the combat bar
and refused by the inventory screen. Restating "what is a heal" in a third place
would have rebuilt that split. All three items he named pass it — Trauma Kit
(45 HP + cure bleed), Trail Rations (6 + 3), Blueberries (4 + 1) — and a pure
stat buff does not. The effect is read from the CATALOG, not the instance, so an
old saved kit racks exactly like a fresh one (the OTA-997 bug on the bandolier).

⚠ THE ✚ heals BUTTON IS ON BOTH ROWS and its popup is NOT gated on combat, which
is the half he asked for by name. The bandolier stays combat-only because a throw
needs something to throw at; a heal is exactly as useful on the walk home, and
the walk home is when you actually patch up. Green where the bandolier is orange:
one rack throws things away from you, one puts you back together, and mid-fight
nobody should have to read the label to know which popup opened.

⚠⚠ ALL THREE RACKS NOW FOLD, THROUGH ONE `RackFrame`. Three banners above the
pack cost real screen on a phone and the healing pouch has just made it three, so
they collapse — but through ONE shared frame rather than three copies of a
chevron, and in the SAME ▸/▾ grammar arb108 gave the inventory categories, so a
player who has learned to fold a category learns nothing new to fold a rack.

  • ⚠ THE COUNT STAYS ON THE HEADER WHEN FOLDED ("2/3 loaded"), which is what
    makes folding safe: the space saved costs no information he was reading the
    banner for. A rack you must unfold to trust is a rack you stop folding.
  • Defaults OPEN, unlike categories, which default closed. A category is one of
    a dozen above a long pack; a rack is one of three whose whole job is to be
    glanceable. Folding is something he does, not a state he inherits.
  • All THREE fill modes are now mutually exclusive — two armed tap modes at once
    is a coin flip over which rack receives the item.

⚠ THE CHEVRON GATE CAUGHT THIS AND WAS RIGHT TO. `RackFrame`'s prop is `open`, so
true means OPEN — the OPPOSITE polarity to the category headers a few hundred
lines above it in the same file, which is exactly the collision check:chevrons
was written for. Registered rather than worked around.

⚠ TWO SUITES WENT RED ON THE FIRST FULL RUN, BOTH FOR THE SAME REASON: ota1097
and ota1100 each hand-typed the TWO-flag fill-mode guard into a string, so making
it three broke tests about fusion-select and the group gesture. Their actual claim
is "a rack fill mode beats this gesture", however many racks exist — both now
assert that over EVERY known fill flag instead of pinning the arity, so the fourth
rack will not break them.

Gates: all 18 green by exit code. Full suite green — 1120 suites, 11,604 tests.
